newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's MRTA rebels enter jungle town - radio.
newsitem.headline: Peru's MRTA rebels enter jungle town - radio.

text.p: About 20 rebels from Peru's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) entered a small jungle village on Friday to demand food and spread propaganda, local radio reported.

In the first such action by the MRTA that has been reported in several months, a rebel unit of 13 men and seven women, all between 17 and 25-years-old, woke up residents of Palcazu, the central Pasco region, around dawn, Cadena Peruana de Noticias (CPN) said.
They proceeded to collect food, give speeches on the reasons for the MRTA takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, and daub slogans on the wall.
"Long live the MRTA!" and "Long live the takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima" read some of the slogans, according to CPN.
The MRTA's armed members, estimated to number anywhere between a few score and 250, are mainly based in Peru's central jungle area.
The 15-strong unit still holding 74 hostages for the 24th day at the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima came from the same region.
The MRTA is demanding the release of its roughly 400 jailed comrades in return for the release of the captives.
